column2: req_desc

Guest save without sign-up
Opening the game without a session creates a guest courier whose stamps, satchels and open parcel are stored on the server and come back on reload in the same browser, as specified in API.

Walk and jump on Bramble
The courier walks, turns and jumps all the way around the planet under gravity that always pulls toward its centre, using keys or the touch controls, and the world region reports position, grounded state and whether a parcel is carried.

Accept a parcel
Taking a parcel from a resident's letter accepts a live standard mission, records the mission version and returns the route from where the courier stands.

Resident letters
Reading a mission or handing a parcel over opens a folded letter from the resident that unfolds from the resident's on-screen position and shows that mission version's offer or thanks lines.

Hand over at the door
A hand-over succeeds only within the door distance set in Business rules and awards the stamps of the mission version the courier accepted.

Retried hand-overs count once
Repeating a hand-over with the same hand-over ticket returns the original successful result unchanged without awarding stamps again, even after a rush hold has lapsed, while error answers are never kept and reusing a ticket for a different hand-over is refused, as qualified in Business rules.

Paired stamp ledger
Every stamp movement is two paired entries that sum to zero, and every balance the API or screen shows, including on every Stamp history page, equals the sum of all the courier's own entries.

Outfitter satchels
Couriers buy satchels with stamps without the balance ever going below zero, even when purchases arrive together, and they can wear any satchel they own, as qualified in Business rules.

Postbox key request
Asking for a postbox key emails a sign-in link and answers every well-formed address with the same status, body and timing, as qualified in Business rules.

Postbox key expiry and single use
A postbox key works once and only within the lifetime set by its environment variable, and used, expired and unknown keys are each refused with their own code.

Guest save claim merges once
Redeeming a postbox key in a guest browser merges that guest save into the courier exactly once, carrying its ledger movements with their original ids and times, its satchels, its stored tickets and its open parcel over without duplicates, and reports what it moved.

Rush board
Couriers see the day's rush parcels on the depot board, each with its status from their own point of view, under a heading that counts the parcels a claim could still win, and signed-in couriers can claim posted ones, as qualified in Business rules.

One winner per rush parcel
When several couriers claim the same rush parcel at once, including the instant a rival's hold lapses, exactly one claim succeeds and every other claimant is refused, sees the parcel taken and has no stamps reserved.

Rush hold expiry
A rush hold ends at the claim's commit time plus the hold length set by its environment variable, and from that instant, judged by the server clock as each request is processed, the hand-over is refused, the parcel is claimable and it returns to the board exactly once, as qualified in Business rules.

Drop a parcel
A courier can drop their own open parcel, which frees their hands and puts a dropped rush parcel straight back on the board, while a delivered, dropped or lapsed parcel can't be dropped.

Horizon thread readout
While a parcel is open, the route status region and the compass ring report remaining arc, bearing, ribbon fraction and route id from the courier's live position, as defined in Business rules.

Horizon thread motion
Taking a parcel plays the camera pull-back to an orbit that frames both the courier and the door, the ribbon unspool and the camera return in order within the time ranges in Motion and effects, and only a confirmed hand-over snaps the compass notch to a stamp.

Reduced-motion route readout
With reduced motion requested, taking a parcel moves no camera, the ribbon appears whole and shortens in tenths, the ring stays still, and the text readout and arrival announcement take their place.

Touch controls
On a touch screen, an on-screen move stick and a jump button let a guest walk, jump, take a parcel and hand it over without a keyboard.

Photo postcard capture
A signed-in courier in photo mode frames the view with the photo camera, which orbits and zooms by the stated steps under drag, pinch, wheel and arrow keys, and takes a postcard of that view, which lands in their postbox with a share link.

Postcard storage integrity
The server reads every chunk of an uploaded postcard and inflates its image data, storing only a structurally sound, still PNG whose pixel data has exactly the size its header promises and that lies within the stated size and dimension limits, refusing each fault with its own reason before anything is stored, and once each upload or revoke has finished a postcard record exists exactly when its stored image exists, as qualified in Business rules.

Postcard share links
Every postcard has an unguessable public link that shows the image to anyone who has it, can't change anything and serves the image with the headers listed in API so browsers never reinterpret it.

Revoke a postcard
Revoking a postcard from the postbox removes its record and its stored image, and its share link stops resolving at once.

Darkroom outage
When the postcard store is unreachable, at boot or later, walking, delivering and the rest of the game keep working while photo mode reports the darkroom closed and the store's actions answer the darkroom-closed response, as qualified in Services.

Mail a postcard
A signed-in courier mails a postcard's share link to one friend within the DP-46 limit, and the email arrives with the From name and subject defined in Services.

Display names stay on one line
Line breaks and control characters in a display name are folded into spaces when it is saved, so a name can never add email headers, recipients or a second subject line.

Post office outage
When the mail server is unreachable, postbox key requests and postcard mail fail with the post-office-closed response and copy while play continues, and a failed postcard mail uses none of the courier's mail allowance.

Shared presence and emotes
Couriers on Bramble see each other's recent positions, satchel colours and emotes within the delay set in Business rules, and the server keeps only the newest heartbeat of each page, ignoring repeated and out-of-order ones.

Presence shows only public fields
Each courier appears at most once in the presence a courier receives, and each entry carries exactly display name, satchel colour, position and emote taken from stored server state, never an email, account id or stamp balance.

Mute a courier
A community helper or the founder mutes or unmutes a courier from the moderation drawer, a repeated mute or unmute is refused, and simultaneous mutes of one courier leave exactly one success, as qualified in Business rules.

Force-rename a courier
A community helper or the founder replaces an abusive courier's display name with a fresh courier name that the courier can't change afterwards.

Helper powers stop at moderation
The server refuses every mission, studio and online-view action from a community helper and every moderation action from an ordinary courier, rather than only hiding the controls.

Moderation audit
Every successful mute, unmute and rename writes exactly one append-only audit entry that keeps the actor's role and name and the target's names as they were at that moment, staff list the entries newest first, and no method can edit or delete one.

Mission drafts with dialogue
The founder writes a mission in the console with its resident, stamp reward, kind and dialogue lines and saves it as a draft without redeploying.

Mission lifecycle
Missions move only along draft, scheduled, live and retired as defined in Business rules, a scheduled mission goes live by itself at the chosen instant within the stated scheduling window, and every illegal move is refused.

Live edits make new versions
Editing a live mission creates a new version for new acceptances and rush claims, while couriers already carrying the parcel finish on the version they accepted or claimed.

Studio time zone and daily board reset
The board date follows the studio time zone's local wall clock, with each board day starting at four in the morning local time, including on daylight-saving change days and in half-hour and 45-minute zones; only exact names from the published zone list are accepted, and a change applies from the next read and re-renders the console's go-live times, as qualified in Business rules.

Who is online
The founder console counts distinct couriers on Bramble now, split into guests and signed in, so that the parts always add up to the total and match the presence list, and the count moves at once on redeem and sign-out, as qualified in Business rules.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from the run manifest, listens on the public port and answers the health check.

Service credentials from environment
Every database, store and mail credential and URL is read from the environment at start, never hard-coded and never sent to the browser.

Server boundary
The server rejects cross-origin writes and oversized or wrongly typed bodies, and never serves source, configuration or credentials, as defined in Server boundary.

Responsive layout
At phone, tablet and laptop sizes, the stamp cards, compass ring and controls take their stated places with no sideways scrolling, and only open dialogs and sheets cover the central clear zone defined in Screens and layout.

Keyboard and focus order
Every control on the game screen, in its cards and dialogs, is reachable in the stated Tab order with a visible focus ring; Escape closes dialogs, and focus returns to the control that opened them.

Risograph paper look
Overlays look like perforated paper stamp-cards on a warm paper ground, with ink type, pink, teal and sun accents and small text pinned to the edges, as described in Visual design.

Procedural world
The planet, the residents' homes, the couriers, the sky scraps, the clouds and the stamp art are all drawn from code (shaders, generated geometry and SVG), with no bundled third-party 3D models or textures.

Postcard mail limit
A courier mails at most the number of postcards Business rules allows in its rolling window, across all their postcards and sessions and even when sends arrive together; the next send is refused with a wait time, and refused and failed sends use no allowance.

Requests carry only published fields
A request body carrying any key its endpoint doesn't publish, at the top level or nested, is refused whole with the unknown-field reason and changes nothing, so a courier can't set their own mute, balance or role, or their presence name or colour, as qualified in Business rules.

Stamp history pages
From the Satchel card, a courier pages through their stamp history newest first by whole movements with a cursor bound to them, so no movement repeats or goes missing while new ones arrive, merged guest movements keep their original time, and every page carries the full balance, as qualified in API.

Postcard copies carry nothing private
Postcard emails and public postcard pages carry only the sender's display name as stored at send or view time and the share link, never the sender's email, any internal id or store detail, and never a Reply-To, Sender, Cc or Bcc header.

Mute and rename reach presence at once
A mute clears the courier's current emote so the next presence read by anyone shows none and other couriers' screens drop the bubble, an unmute never revives an emote sent before or during the mute, and a rename shows on the next read.

Intro camera dive
Each load of the game opens with a camera dive from the stated far view of the whole planet down to the resting over-the-shoulder pose, always getting closer, within the stated time range; any key press or tap skips it at once, and reduced motion replaces it with a still start.

Ambient sky motion
Drifting paper scraps and a slowly orbiting ring of clouds move around Bramble while the page is visible, pause in place while it is hidden and stay still under reduced motion, with the state exposed on the world region.

Upright courier and following camera
The courier stands upright on the sphere everywhere and eases into and out of turns, and the follow camera rests at the stated distance, height, look-ahead and field of view and settles there within the stated range without ever dipping below the surface clearance.

Other couriers glide and fade
Other couriers glide between presence updates rather than jumping and fade in and out when they arrive or leave, each figure stays matched to its courier by the stated rule so a rename or redeem changes its tag in place, and under reduced motion they move and appear at once.

Interrupted animations stay continuous
An action taken while an animation is playing continues or reverses that animation from its current visual state without a jump, and every queued change, such as two balance changes in a row, plays in turn and ends on the server's value.

Hidden tab resumes in phase
When the page is hidden during a timed sequence and then shown again, each sequence picks up in the phase that matches the time that has passed, while ambient motion resumes from where it paused.

Notice motion
Each new notice fades in and slides down a few pixels in about a fifth of a second, or appears at once under reduced motion, and its phase is exposed on the Notices region.

Services reconnect without restart
Every request that needs the postcard store or the mail server tries it afresh, reusing a cached failure only for the time stated in Server boundary, so a returning service works again without a server restart.

A double-tapped purchase buys once
Every satchel purchase carries a purchase ticket, so repeating it returns the original result unchanged and buys once, reusing it for another satchel is refused, refusals are never kept, and tickets travel with a claimed guest save, as qualified in Business rules.

Another courier's parcel is invisible
Dropping or handing over a parcel that belongs to another courier answers exactly like a parcel that never existed and changes nothing, and no response ever shows a courier another courier's parcel id.

Hand-over state is honest
While a hand-over or rush claim is waiting for the server, the screen shows it as pending and never as delivered or won, a retried hand-over resends the same ticket and body, and each server answer moves the thread to its stated phase, as qualified in Interactions.

Studio-time scheduling across clock changes
The founder schedules a mission in studio wall-clock time, and the server refuses times the clocks skip, resolves times that happen twice to the earlier instant, and keeps the resolved instant when the studio zone changes.

Console is keyboard-complete
The founder can create, edit, schedule and move missions with the keyboard alone in the stated Tab order, with focus landing on the stated control after each save, error and move and never disturbed by the console refresh.

Stale console edits are refused
Every change to a mission must name the revision it was made from, so an edit or move made from an out-of-date view is refused and changes nothing, and of simultaneous edits from one revision exactly one succeeds.

The thread is really drawn
The route ribbon is drawn on screen in the route teal next to the recipient's door while a parcel is open and is gone from there shortly after the parcel closes, matching the door position the Route region reports.

Old session cookies stop working
Redeeming a postbox key always issues a new session and signing out ends the old one, so a copied earlier session cookie is refused everywhere from then on.

A repeated accept or claim returns the parcel you carry
Repeating an accept of the mission a courier already carries, or a claim of the rush parcel they hold, answers with that parcel exactly as first returned, creates nothing and never extends the hold, while any other accept or claim with full hands is refused, as qualified in Business rules.

A lapsed hold is noticed without a hand-over
While a rush parcel is open, the screen notices its hold has lapsed from a Me read at the hold end or the next board refresh, rewinds the thread, shows the row as Claim or Taken and announces the lapse exactly once within 11 seconds of the hold end, as qualified in Interactions.

Display names are measured as Unicode text
A display name holding a lone surrogate is refused, and any other is folded, trimmed, normalised to NFC and counted in Unicode code points against the 1 to 24 limit, and it reaches the friend's email exactly through encoded headers, as qualified in Business rules.

Signed-out and claimed couriers leave presence at once
Signing out or claiming a guest save removes that session from presence and Online now on the very next read, while a courier still playing in another session stays listed once at that session's newest position, and other couriers' screens show a redeemed browser as one figure whose tag changes in place.

The console editor lives in the URL
The console URL names the mission in the editor, so a reload, a copied URL and Back and Forward reopen it, an unknown mission is reported, and leaving unsaved edits by Back or Forward asks first, as qualified in Interactions.

Taking a parcel waits for the depot
While an accept is waiting for the depot, the offer letter stays open with Take the parcel disabled and no camera move, ribbon, carried parcel or route id appears; only a 201 or 200 folds the letter and starts the thread, and a refusal folds it with its copy and draws no thread, as qualified in Interactions.

A postbox key only returns to Bramble's own pages
A postbox key request may name one of the listed Bramble paths to return to, any other value is refused before any key or email is made, and the claim page's way back follows only the stored path, never a query parameter or another origin.

Every rush parcel has its own number and name
Each rush row carries its fixed parcel number and its mission's posted count for that board date, keeps them through drops, lapses, same-day slot edits and retires, and its Claim button is named 'Claim <title>, parcel <slot> of <slots>', unique on the board, while simultaneous claims on different parcels of one mission all win.

Reduced motion can change mid-walk
A change to the device's reduced-motion preference while the page is open switches every motion to its stated mode within half a second, in either direction, without a reload and without replaying the thread, as qualified in Motion and effects.

Outages and faults never describe the machinery
No response body or header, status read, share page or screen copy ever names the store or mail server's address as defined in Server boundary, the bucket, an object key, a driver or socket error or a stack frame, unexpected faults answer the fixed internal error, and no response carries X-Powered-By or a Server header.

A retried postcard mail sends once
Every postcard mail carries a mail ticket, so a repeat returns the original answer before any not-found, limit or outage answer without sending or using a slot, a ticket reused for another postcard or friend is refused, and simultaneous duplicates yield identical answers and one email, as qualified in Business rules.

The moderation drawer is keyboard-complete
In the moderation drawer the keyboard reaches every row's toggle and Rename in the stated order, and after each mute, unmute, refused repeat, rename, reload or departure focus lands on the stated control and never on the page body, as qualified in Interactions.
/app/run.json exists and contains exactly the string keys _schema (value run-manifest-v1), install, build and serve.

/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md names every shipped package with its version and licence, plus Fraunces, Atkinson Hyperlegible and Lucide; shipped packages means the production dependency tree as reported by npm ls --omit=dev --all --json.

Every shipped package (the production dependency tree, as reported by npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) and every bundled font, icon or asset is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, Zlib, CC0-1.0 or OFL-1.1.
The only datastores are the provided Postgres database, the MinIO bucket and Mailpit; there is no SQLite, Redis, embedded database or state file on disk.
The provided service configuration (compose fragments and service environment values) is left unchanged.
Server and browser application source is TypeScript; JavaScript appears only as build output or tool configuration.
